phys-qm-01-c1.text: NIST (CODATA Task Group on Fundamental Constants) (2022). Fundamental Physical Constants: Planck constant. NIST Reference on Constants, Units, and Uncertainty.
MIT Department of Physics (2024). The Photoelectric Effect (Junior Lab experiment guide). MIT Department of Physics, 8.13 Experimental Physics.
phys-qm-01-c1.quote: The 1921 Nobel Prize was awarded to Albert Einstein for his discovery of “the law of photoelectric effect”.
phys-qm-01-c1.claim: Einstein took it seriously and used it to explain the photoelectric effect (1905), which won him the Nobel Prize.

phys-qm-01-c2.text: Richard Fitzpatrick. Electron Diffraction (Quantum Mechanics lecture notes). University of Texas at Austin, Physics 355.
phys-qm-01-c2.quote: electrons scattered by the surface of a nickel metal crystal display a diffraction pattern
phys-qm-01-c2.claim: by diffracting electrons off a nickel crystal, so electrons interfere like waves

phys-qm-01-c3.text: Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, Marlan O. Scully, Dudley R. Herschbach (2014). Bohr's molecular model, a century later. Physics Today (AIP).
phys-qm-01-c3.quote: His concluding and most familiar version invoked stationary circular orbits specified by quantized orbital angular momentum,
phys-qm-01-c3.claim: In 1913 Bohr proposed that electrons can only occupy certain allowed orbits with quantised angular momentum.

phys-qm-02-c1.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1954). Max Born - Facts. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-02-c1.quote: for his fundamental research in quantum mechanics, especially for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction
phys-qm-02-c1.claim: The probability of finding the particle in a small region dx is |ψ|² dx.

phys-qm-02-c2.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1933). Erwin Schrödinger - Facts. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-02-c2.quote: in 1926 Erwin Schrödinger formulated a wave equation that accurately calculated the energy levels of electrons in atoms.
phys-qm-02-c2.claim: Schrödinger (1926) wrote the equation governing how wavefunctions evolve in time

phys-qm-02-c3.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1932). Werner Heisenberg - Facts. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-02-c3.quote: In 1927 he proposed the “uncertainty relation”, setting limits for how precisely the position and velocity of a particle can be simultaneously determined.
phys-qm-02-c3.claim: Heisenberg (1927) proved that position and momentum cannot both be known precisely simultaneously

phys-qm-03-c1.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (2022). The Nobel Prize in Physics 2022 (press release). NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-03-c1.quote: When he took the measurements, they supported quantum mechanics by clearly violating a Bell inequality. This means that quantum mechanics cannot be replaced by a theory that uses hidden variables.
phys-qm-03-c1.claim: Experimental violations of Bell inequalities rule out any local hidden-variable explanation.

phys-qm-03-c2.text: Jeffrey Barrett (2023). Everettian Quantum Mechanics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-qm-03-c2.quote: Everett proposed dropping the collapse dynamics (rule 4b) from the standard collapse theory
phys-qm-03-c2.claim: Many-Worlds says all outcomes happen, in branching universes.

phys-qm-03-c2.text: Sheldon Goldstein (2021). Bohmian Mechanics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-qm-03-c2.quote: in Bohmian mechanics the configuration of a system of particles evolves via a deterministic motion choreographed by the wave function.
phys-qm-03-c2.claim: Pilot wave theory says there are hidden variables guiding a definite particle.

phys-qm-03-c3.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1943). Otto Stern - Facts. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-03-c3.quote: In a 1922 experiment, Otto Stern and Walter Gerlach passed a beam of silver atoms through an inhomogeneous magnetic field.
phys-qm-03-c3.claim: The Stern-Gerlach experiment (1922) sent silver atoms through an inhomogeneous magnetic field

phys-qm-04-c1.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (2022). The Nobel Prize in Physics 2022 (press release). NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-04-c1.quote: This means that quantum mechanics cannot be replaced by a theory that uses hidden variables.
phys-qm-04-c1.claim: Bell's theorem and subsequent experiments proved Einstein wrong.

phys-qm-04-c2.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (2022). The Nobel Prize in Physics 2022 (press release). NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-04-c2.quote: Alain Aspect developed the setup, using it in a way that closed an important loophole.
phys-qm-04-c2.claim: Alain Aspect's experiments (1982) definitively showed Bell inequality violations

phys-qm-04-c3.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (2022). The Nobel Prize in Physics 2022 (press release). NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-04-c3.quote: quantum teleportation, which makes it possible to move a quantum state from one particle to one at a distance.
phys-qm-04-c3.claim: Quantum teleportation (Bennett et al. 1993) uses an entangled pair to transfer a quantum state from Alice to Bob.

phys-qm-05-c1.text: Amit Hagar and Michael Cuffaro (2019). Quantum Computing. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-qm-05-c1.quote: P. W. Shor (1994) who showed how a quantum algorithm apparently can factor large numbers into primes far more efficiently than any known classical algorithm.
phys-qm-05-c1.claim: Shor's algorithm factors large numbers exponentially faster than classical algorithms

phys-qm-06-c3.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1986). The Nobel Prize in Physics 1986. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-06-c3.quote: Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer for their design of the scanning tunneling microscope
phys-qm-06-c3.claim: Binnig and Rohrer won the 1986 Nobel for STM.

phys-qm-07-c1.text: Richard P. Feynman (1965). Nobel Lecture: The Development of the Space-Time View of Quantum Electrodynamics. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-07-c1.quote: for each possible way that the particle can go from one point to another in space-time, there’s an amplitude. That amplitude is e to the times the action for the path. Amplitudes from various paths superpose by addition.
phys-qm-07-c1.claim: In Feynman's formulation, the amplitude for a particle to go from A to B is a sum over all possible paths connecting them

phys-qm-08-c1.text: Jan Faye (2019). Copenhagen Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-qm-08-c1.quote: complementarity was established as the orthodox interpretation of quantum mechanics in the 1930s

phys-qm-08-c2.text: Jeffrey Barrett (2023). Everettian Quantum Mechanics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-qm-08-c2.quote: Hugh Everett III proposed solving the quantum measurement problem by adopting pure wave mechanics, the theory one gets by dropping the collapse dynamics from the standard von Neumann formulation of quantum mechanics.

phys-qm-08-c3.text: Sheldon Goldstein (2021). Bohmian Mechanics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-qm-08-c3.quote: in Bohmian mechanics the configuration of a system of particles evolves via a deterministic motion choreographed by the wave function.
phys-qm-08-c3.claim: Pilot wave / Bohmian: particles have definite positions guided by a real wavefunction.

phys-qm-06-c1.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1973). Ivar Giaever - Facts. NobelPrize.org.
phys-qm-06-c1.quote: particles can pass through barriers that they should not be able to squeeze through according to classic physics.
phys-qm-06-c1.claim: Classically, a particle without enough energy to surmount a potential barrier simply bounces off.
